name: Mbói Tu'ĩ
prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Mbói Tu'ĩ, the colossal Guaraní serpent-parrot guardian of wetlands.
ANATOMY: ONE PARROT HEAD with curved beak, TWO eyes, long RED FORKED TONGUE; long scaled SERPENT BODY with feathers only on head/back; EXACTLY TWO short LEGS attached near torso, each ending birdlike foot. NO wings, NO forearms, NO extra legs. [mboi-tu-i-c05,mboi-tu-i-c08,mboi-tu-i-c13]
MOMENT: Rear from great marsh, two feet clutch separate rocks, parrot beak open with forked red tongue visible, serpent coils thrust forward.
POWER: Heavy storm rain moves across wetland as documented storm calling; body displaces real water; no aura, illness depicted or invented lightning attack. [mboi-tu-i-c06]
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle, subject fills80% of square; natural scale unless giant explicitly documented. Important features clear at200pixels.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one dominant warm moonbreak/sunset or storm gap, strong rim light, deep walnut shadows, ordinary physical dust/moisture.
SURFACE: tactile natural fur/skin/scales where appropriate, coarse opaque textiles, rough stone, original visible painterly brushwork.
SETTING: Great marsh and rocks/crags near Tobatí and Cavaju hill. [mboi-tu-i-c08,mboi-tu-i-c11]
MOOD: dangerous for hostile beings, awe-inspiring and respectful for gods/guardians, uncanny audacious for benign small spirits, never cute/calm/decorative.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text/lettering/logo/border/frame/watermark; no extra heads/limbs/fingers; no borrowed film/game/anime/comic design; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outlines, energy ribbons, floating runes.

rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and head/beak, tongue-fork, feathered-back, coil, and both foot crops. One parrot head (mboi-tu-i-c02/c05) with a hooked macaw beak, seen in profile with one eye; the second eye is on the hidden side, not missing. The beak is wide open, and a long red tongue splits into exactly two forked tips (c05). Red, yellow and green feathers cover the head and lie along the back only (c05). The feathered mantle lies flat on the back and ends at the scaled body, so it is not a wing: there are no wings and no forearms. The body is a long scaled serpent whose coils loop through the water behind and under the torso (c05/c08). It has EXACTLY TWO legs on the torso (c05), each a scaled bird foot gripping a separate wet rock with curved talons. The colossal creature (c08/c13) rears over a low camera out of a great marsh (c11). Storm rain lashes the marsh under black clouds with one sunset gap (calls storms, c06), and the body throws up real splash. A crag and a hill rise behind (rocks and crags, Cavaju hill, c08/c11). No illness, victims, text or aura. It reads as a fearsome yet grand wetland guardian, strong at 200px. Original design.
